original: Figma effect styles, same in both modes
reason: Shadows are invisible on near-black surfaces and only add haze. In dark mode elevation is a lighter surface (raised 850) plus a border.

original: Cool blue-grey ramp (colors-neutral-*), reused for dark
ours: colors-neutral-dark-25 … 950: a green-tinted ramp (OKLCH hue 172, chroma 0.004–0.016)
reason: Figma Dark reuses the light neutral ramp, a blue-grey that clashes with the green brand and makes dark mode look off-brand. The tinted ramp keeps the same lightness steps.

ours: Unchanged for buttons and --background-*: primary 600, success 700, info 600, warning 700, error 600
reason: The label on these fills is white in both modes, and a lighter step (400–500) drops white text below 4.5:1 (3.2–3.9:1). Kept on purpose. Badges, tags, status tags, alerts and featured icons do not use these: they get the soft tints logged under Dark theme.
Typo: Wieght → Weight. Only the Figma group name was wrong.

original: The Figma variable holds the font style name: Regular, Medium, Semibold, Bold.
reason: CSS needs a number or a keyword: font-weight: Semibold is invalid, so font-medium, font-semibold and font-bold all fell back to 400 and every label, heading and tab rendered regular. Found while building the Phase 4 components, and fixed for all of them.

original: Not defined. Figma has Desktop, Tablet and Mobile modes with no pixel widths.
reason: These are the widths the design.dga.gov.sa CSS uses and also Tailwind's defaults. Figma's tablet frame is 704 + 2×32 = 768px wide, which matches md.

original: tokens.css (extraction guess): Desktop default, Tablet at max-width 1024px, Mobile at max-width 640px
ours: Mobile-first: Mobile is the base, Tablet from 768px (md), Desktop from 1024px (lg)
reason: Mobile-first matches Tailwind's min-width breakpoints, and 768px is where Figma's tablet grid starts.

original: Mobile mode: text-md 12px, text-sm 10px, text-xs 8px; Tablet: text-md 14px
ours: Body text sizes stay at their desktop values on every viewport. Display sizes still follow the Figma modes.
reason: 8–12px body text is hard to read on phones, iOS zooms into inputs under 16px, and the mobile mode made text-lg (14px) smaller than text-md.

original: Token line heights 1.4 to 1.6 and -2% letter spacing on display sizes, for every language
ours: In Arabic: line height 1.8 for body text and 1.5 for headings, letter spacing 0 on every element.
reason: The marks above and below Arabic letters need more room than the Latin line heights give, and negative tracking breaks the joins between letters. Latin text keeps the Figma values.

item: Site CSS vs Figma (39 material conflicts, 87 rounding-only, shadow-sm)
reason: Figma is the source of truth. The full list is in tokens/TOKEN_CONFLICTS.md.

ours: Dropped. rounded-2xl, rounded-3xl and rounded-4xl clamp to radius-xl (24px) so shadcn class names still work.
reason: Not in Figma, and it clashes with the Figma scale (site radius-2xl is 16px, the same as Figma radius-lg).
Figma is the source of truth. Only shadow-sm differed (5% vs 6%/10% opacity).

ours: [data-theme="dark"] and .dark (both work, also on any subtree)
reason: shadcn and next-themes use the .dark class. All semantic tokens are re-declared in the dark scope so nested dark sections resolve correctly.

original: shadcn derives radius-sm…4xl from --radius with calc()
ours: Fixed DGA radii: none 0, xs 2, sm 4, md 8, lg 16, xl 24, full 9999px; --radius = radius-sm (4px)
reason: DGA defines exact radii. Buttons and inputs use radius-sm (4px).

ours: Tailwind's --spacing: 0.25rem, so p-4 = 16px and p-80 = 320px, matching DGA one-to-one
reason: rem keeps spacing in step with the user's root font size. The raw --spacing-* variables keep their px values.

ours: Every state of every component, on each surface it can sit on, in light and dark mode (scripts/tokens/components.ts). Phase 2: Button, Spinner, Link, Badge, Tag, Avatar and Featured Icon.
reason: Foundation pairs alone miss component states such as hovered labels and on-colour fills. Each component page lists its checks.

original: Flips to white in dark mode
reason: It is an inverse surface (white in dark mode), so text on it must use the inverse colour, not text-oncolor-primary. Primary-neutral buttons use button-background-black-*, which stays dark.

ours: Use only on deep fills: nav header, pressed/selected primary, black. On mid-tone fills use --text-oncolor-primary.
reason: White itself is only 4.57–4.83:1 on the 600-level fills, so no lower opacity can pass there. On deep fills 80% and 70% white pass AA.

original: Not in the DGA Figma file. Defined only in the design.dga.gov.sa CSS (.featured-icon).
ours: Built from the site CSS: hard, light and outlined; brand, neutral, success, error, warning and info; sm 32, md 40, lg 48 and xl 56px; square or circle.
reason: Figma is the source of truth where it exists; here only the site CSS does.

item: Featured Icon: hard warning and success
original: Hard warning: white on warning-400. Hard success: white on brand-600 (the same as brand).
ours: Hard warning uses yellow-700; hard success uses green-700 (DGA status green).
reason: White on yellow-400 is 1.9:1, below the 3:1 non-text minimum. Success uses the status palette so it differs from brand, as the site's semantic block (text-success) does.

original: Five composite Skeleton Components (Image Button and Text, Icon and List, Image Content and Button, Chart and Content, Image Profile Content and Button)
ours: One Skeleton primitive (rectangle, square, circle, line) and the five layouts as copy-paste examples on the docs page
reason: The composites are layouts of the primitives; real pages need their own shapes.
A gentle pulse shows that content is loading. prefers-reduced-motion turns it off.

original: Neutral, Primary, Alpha-white and White, with no colour tokens in the export
ours: neutral → border-neutral-secondary, primary → border-primary, alpha-white → border-oncolor-transparent-30, white → icon-oncolor (white in both modes)
reason: Mapped to the closest semantic border tokens. border-white flips to black in dark mode, so white uses a token that stays white.

original: Initials use Text xs/Semibold on every size in the export
ours: Text style per size from the site CSS: 24 Text 2xs Bold, 32 Text xs SemiBold, 40 Text sm SemiBold, 48 Text md SemiBold, 64 Text xl Medium, 80 Display sm, 120 Display md
reason: One text size cannot fit avatars from 24 to 120px.

original: Text 2xs/SemiBold on every size in the exported variant table
ours: Text sm (md, 32px), Text xs (sm, 24px) and Text 2xs (xs, 20px), SemiBold
reason: The export lists one sample text style. A 10px label in a 32px tag is hard to read; the sizes follow the site CSS (.tag--lg uses 14px).

ours: onDismiss adds a trailing close button (Cancel icon) with an aria-label (dismissLabel). The tag itself is not interactive.
reason: Removable filter tags need a real button for keyboard and screen-reader users.

original: Ghost: neutral label with no fill
ours: Every status tag starts with a coloured dot (tag-icon-*; tag-dot on inverted) so ghost tags still show their colour.
reason: Ghost tags would otherwise all look the same; the dot is decorative and the label carries the status.

original: Not in the DGA Figma file. Defined only in the design.dga.gov.sa CSS (.badge).
ours: Built from the site CSS: sizes sm 20, md 24 and lg 32px, filled and outlined, square and rounded, icon-only. Colours map to DGA palettes (brand → success, purple → lavender).
reason: The badge is used across DGA sites. Figma is the source of truth where it exists; here only the site CSS does.
DGA has no pink palette, in Figma or in the token set.
White 90% on the brand fill is 4.16:1; white is 4.57:1 or better.

original: Focused: border-black stroke (border-white on colour). Disabled: a separate variant.
ours: 2px outline on :focus-visible with a 2px offset (white on colour, both modes). disabled removes the href and sets aria-disabled.
reason: Keyboard-only focus (WCAG 2.4.7). A link without an href cannot be followed or focused.

ours: external opens a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer", shows the external-link icon (mirrored in RTL) and adds "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers.
reason: WCAG 3.2.5: warn before opening a new window.

original: Figma defines only the Default state for destructive buttons (Primary, Secondary-Solid, Secondary-Outline, Subtle, Transparent).
ours: Hovered, pressed, selected, focused and disabled follow the same pattern as the non-destructive styles, using the button-background-danger-* tokens (which already have every state).
reason: A button needs every state. The danger fill tokens exist in Figma for all states.

ours: variant="neutral" with destructive renders as destructive primary
reason: Figma has no neutral destructive style. Falling back keeps every prop combination valid.

original: Focused is a separate Figma state with a 2px border-black (border-white on colour) stroke inside the button.
ours: Shown on :focus-visible only (keyboard), as a 2px outline outside the button with a 1px inner ring in the button's surface colour. On-colour buttons use white (icon-oncolor) in both modes.
reason: WCAG 2.4.7 / 2.4.11. An outside outline does not shift the label, and border-white flips to black in dark mode (2.11:1 on the nav header).

original: Hovered, pressed and selected change the label to green-400/300
ours: The label stays white; hovered and selected add an underline, pressed adds an underline and 80% opacity.
reason: Colour alone cannot meet 4.5:1 on the brand fill (see the label token fixes).

ours: Applied with aria-pressed="true" (toggle buttons) or data-selected
reason: Screen readers announce aria-pressed; data-selected covers buttons in menus and groups.

ours: loading prop: a Spinner replaces the leading icon, the width is kept, aria-busy is set and the button is disabled for clicks but stays focusable.
reason: Async actions need a busy state. Keeping focus avoids losing the user's place.

original: No Field component. Label, helper text and error are parts of each input page.
ours: One Field wraps every control: Label (with required or optional marker), Description (helper text) and Error. Built on Base UI Field, so the label names the control and helper and error text are linked with aria-describedby.
reason: The same three parts appear on every control page. One component keeps them consistent and wires the accessibility attributes once.

item: Field: error is never colour alone
original: Error state is a red border and a message with an icon swap.
ours: aria-invalid on the control, a red border and a message that always starts with an alert icon. Checkbox, radio and switch show the message the same way.
reason: WCAG 1.4.1: colour must not be the only cue. A border colour change alone fails it.

original: A read-only field shows no change when it is focused.
ours: A focused read-only field shows the border colour change and the full underline (no shadow). Its fill and rest border are the DGA ones.
reason: A read-only field is still in the tab order, and a focused element needs a visible indicator (WCAG 2.4.7). Without an outline, the underline is the indicator.

ours: The same, kept as DGA draws it. The value text is 4.5:1 or better.
reason: Not remapped: #d2d6db is 1.5:1 on white, below the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11 if the boundary is needed to find the control. A read-only field shows a value, is not edited, and is named by its label, so the boundary is not what identifies it. Teams that treat read-only fields as controls should use a plain text display instead.

item: Input, Textarea, Select: filled lighter and darker at rest
original: No border at rest, the border on hover, focus and press. The fills are #fcfcfd and #f3f4f6.
ours: The same, kept as DGA draws it. The border is transparent at rest (not removed), so the box does not shift when it appears.
reason: Not remapped: the fills are 1.0:1 and 1.1:1 against the page, below the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11 for the resting boundary. The label, the placeholder (4.5:1 or better) and the hover, focus and press border identify the field. Use the default fill where the field must be findable at rest.

original: Large only: one fixed height (124px sample).
ours: Grows in height (rows, default 4) and the user can resize it vertically; resize can be turned off.
reason: A multi-line field has no single right height. Figma's Resize and Scroll Bar props map to resize and the native scroll bar.

original: Only the open list (Dropdown List Item) is drawn, no popup surface.
ours: A popup on the card surface with a 1px border, as wide as the trigger, opening below it. A 2px bar on the highlighted option (as well as the tint) and a check mark on the chosen one.
reason: The tint alone is 1.1:1 against the popup, so keyboard users could not see which option is highlighted (WCAG 2.4.7).
Named after the Base UI part and the shadcn convention, so it is found when people search for it. The docs page says it is DGA's Dropdown Input.

ours: The field is dir="ltr" with unicode-bidi: isolate, so digits and signs never reorder. Typing or pasting Arabic-Indic (٣) or Persian (۳) digits gives Western digits (3). The − and + buttons sit on the logical start and end.
reason: Numbers are technical values (amounts, IDs, quantities) that must not be reordered or mixed with other digit systems in one field.

original: A trailing icon variant (clear or voice).
ours: A real clear button (24px target, named by clearLabel) that appears when there is text and returns focus to the field. type=search, so Escape clears it too.
reason: Icon-only controls need a name and a keyboard path.

item: Checkbox, Radio: hover and pressed fill in dark mode
original: The checked fill lightens on hover and press.
ours: The fill stays green-600 in dark mode. Hover and press add a background to the box.
reason: A white mark on the lighter fill is 1.4–2.1:1 (see the control-primary-hovered and -pressed fixes).

ours: control-border (3:1), transparent fill, grey mark, and the pointer stays an arrow.
reason: The pale border is 1.5:1 on white. A read-only control keeps a 3:1 boundary.

original: A dash variant of the primary and neutral styles.
ours: indeterminate prop (and aria-checked=mixed). The dash and check mark share one icon slot.
reason: A parent checkbox needs to report a partly selected group to screen readers.

original: A 2px border-black outline on the label's hit box.
ours: A 2px outline 2px outside the control, on :focus-visible only (white in dark mode).
reason: Keyboard-only focus (WCAG 2.4.7). The outline follows the control's shape and does not shift the label.

original: #ccc on the site, no token in Figma.
ours: control-border for the off track, a white thumb, and a tick in the thumb when icon is set.
reason: #ccc is 1.6:1 on white. control-border is 4.8:1, so the off track and its white thumb pass 3:1.

original: An alert message below the label.
ours: The same message with its icon, and a 2px error outline on the off track.
reason: The error must be visible on the control as well as in the text, without relying on colour alone.

original: Single and Multiple variants with a Drop Zone and File parts; drag-over style on the site.
ours: One component for both: a drop zone that is a real file input (Tab, then Space or Enter), a file list with remove, progress and error states, and file-type, size and count validation.
reason: A drop zone that only accepts a mouse drag is not keyboard accessible (WCAG 2.1.1). Rejected files stay in the list with the reason.

ours: Each name has dir="auto" and is wrapped in <bdi>, so an Arabic name reads right to left and "report.pdf" left to right, whatever the page direction. Sizes and percentages are always left to right Western digits.
reason: A name mixing Arabic and Latin text must not be reordered around its extension.

original: Modal: a 600px card (padding 24, radius-md, shadow-3xl). No close button, focus or keyboard behaviour is specified; width: 100% on mobile.
ours: Dialog (DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogClose). A close button in the corner, Escape, a focus trap, focus returning to the trigger, an inert page behind it, sm 400 / md 600 / lg 800px, and 16px of page padding on phones.
reason: A window that takes over the page must be operable by keyboard and announced (WAI-ARIA dialog pattern, WCAG 2.1.1, 2.4.3). Built on Base UI Dialog.

item: Drawer: from Slideout Menu to a modal drawer
original: Slideout Menu: a 346px side panel (.sidepanel) with a physical border-right, always visible in the layout.
ours: Drawer: a modal panel that slides in from the start, end, top or bottom. start and end follow the page direction, the edge border is logical (border-e or border-s) and a touch swipe closes it. White or gray (neutral-100).
reason: A panel that covers the page needs the same focus trap and Escape as a dialog. DGA's border-right and its slide direction are physical, so they would be on the wrong side in Arabic.

original: A 240px bubble with a 14px physical margin per direction (margin-right for left, margin-left for right) and a beak placement and alignment from Figma. Shown on hover.
ours: side is top, bottom, start or end, so start and end swap on Arabic pages and the beak follows. It opens on hover and on keyboard focus, stays open while the pointer is over it, and closes with Escape (WCAG 1.4.13). The Help Icon is TooltipHelp: a 20px button with an accessible name that opens the same bubble as a popover on hover, focus, click and touch.
reason: A tooltip that shows only on hover is invisible to keyboard users, and a physical margin would sit on the wrong side in RTL. Base UI also advises that an info icon whose purpose is to show the text be a popover, so touch and screen reader users can read it.

original: .menu-item:hover is defined twice with different fills (neutral-100 and button-background-neutral-hovered); focus is a 2px black border; disabled is opacity .5.
ours: The Figma fills: button-background-neutral-hovered and -pressed, background-primary-50 for the selected item. Focus is a 2px outline, drawn inside the item and only for keyboard focus. Disabled uses text-default-disabled and icon-default-disabled instead of opacity.
reason: Figma is the source of truth where the CSS disagrees with itself. Opacity on the whole item also fades the focus ring.

original: Five trail variants: Text, Button, Tag, Switch and Icon.
ours: MenuShortcut for text and any element you place after the label (Tag, Switch, an icon). Submenus (MenuSub) and checkbox and radio items are added, with a check mark or a dot on the end side.
reason: One slot covers every trail variant and the extra items cover the menus that apps actually need.

item: Tabs: selected, hover and More tab
original: A 3px bar for hover, press and selected on vertical tabs; a Closed and Open More tab on horizontal tabs.
ours: A 3px bar under (or beside) the selected tab in border-primary; vertical tabs also show a neutral bar on hover and press. A list that does not fit scrolls sideways. The More tab (an overflow menu) is not built: compose a Menu in the last tab.
reason: A scrolling list needs no extra control and keeps every tab reachable with Tab and the arrow keys. The overflow menu is on the roadmap.

item: Tabs, Content Switcher: arrow keys in RTL
ours: Left and Right swap on Arabic pages (Base UI DirectionProvider, set from the dir attribute of html by the components themselves), so the arrow that points at the next tab moves to it.
reason: The arrow keys must match what the eyes see, in both directions (WAI-ARIA tabs pattern).

item: Accordion: RTL padding, flush and disabled
original: Body padding in physical sides with two [dir=rtl] overrides per variant; flush draws its line with a border-image gradient at 16px and 382px; disabled is neutral-300 with !important.
ours: Logical padding (ps and pe), so no RTL overrides are needed; flush is a 16px margin on each side of the line (the width follows the container); disabled uses text-default-disabled.
reason: The CSS needs twelve rules where logical properties need none, and the gradient hard-codes a 382px width.

original: Figma has two to three items with a white label (text-oncolor-primary) and an OnColor variant. The CSS only sets margin: 10px.
ours: A neutral-100 track with the chosen option in the primary fill and a white label; one option is always chosen. On a brand fill the track is a translucent black (not white) and the chosen option is white with a dark green label.
reason: White on a white-lightened brand fill is 3.34:1 (down to 2.81:1 pressed); a darkened track keeps 4.5:1 or better, as the on-colour buttons do.

item: Toast: neutral bar, timing and live region
original: Notification Toast: an 8px bar in the kind's 400 colour (white for neutral, so invisible), no timing or announcement.
ours: A bar on the logical start in the kind's 400 colour (neutral uses border-neutral-primary), an icon and a title for each kind, a close button and an optional action. It is announced (polite; assertive for error and warning), pauses while hovered or focused, and can be swiped away. Toaster sits at the bottom end of the screen.
reason: A message that disappears must be announced and must not vanish while someone is reading it (WCAG 4.1.3, 2.2.1).

original: The icon is icon-oncolor (white) on a 50 tint, and the success style uses the brand green where the other kinds use their own colour.
ours: The icon uses the kind's icon colour (3:1 or better on the tint); success uses the success tokens like the Figma fill and text.
reason: A white icon on a 50 tint is 1.0 to 1.1:1: it cannot be seen. The kinds should read as one set.

ours: critical (Notification) and destructive or warning (Inline Alert) are role=alert, the rest role=status, and each hides itself when dismissed.
reason: A message that appears on its own must be announced without moving focus (WCAG 4.1.3). Urgent kinds interrupt; the rest wait.

item: Inline Alert: icon colour and neutral bar
original: The tinted info and warning alerts with a close button use icon-default for the icon, and the neutral bar is white.
ours: The icon is always the kind's icon colour, and the neutral bar is border-neutral-primary. A tinted alert takes the kind's text colour for the title and the text.
reason: The icon should not change when a close button is added, and a white bar on a white alert is not there.

item: Figma variant names: Meduim, Sahdow, Upcomming, Lable
original: Pagination Size "Meduim"; Card Effect "With Sahdow"; Progress Indicator State "Upcomming"; Structured List "Lable AR".
ours: md, shadow, upcoming, label. Sizes are sm, md and lg like every other component.
reason: Typos in the Figma variant names. Prop values in code are spelled correctly.

original: Upcoming: ring, number and title in stepper-button-upcomming (gray-300, #d2d6db), and the Vertical upcoming title in stepper-line-upcomming. 1.48:1 on white.
ours: Ring icon-default-500 (4.78:1), number text-primary-paragraph, title stepper-text-tertiary. The connector line keeps the DGA gray.
reason: Text needs 4.5:1 and a state indicator 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.11). The DGA gray is fine for the decorative line, not for the number, title or ring.

item: Stepper: error state, radial form and CSS
original: Progress Indicator has Current, Completed and Upcomming; the Radial Stepper is a separate component. The CSS hard-codes --colors-brand-600 and a 62px vertical circle for the contribution stepper.
ours: Stepper has completed, current, upcoming and error (a red circle with an alert icon and the title in text-error). Below the sm width a horizontal stepper folds into the Radial Stepper form: a ring with the step count, the step's name and the next one. The brand tokens are used, not the hex.
reason: A process with a problem step needs a state (WCAG 3.3.1), and a nine-step horizontal stepper does not fit a phone. Each step also says its state in words for screen readers, not just by colour.

item: Progress: bar height, status icon and indeterminate
original: Progress Bar frames are 320x50, 56 and 68 for Small, Medium and Large; the bar's own height, the track colour and an indeterminate state are not given. Success and Error variants show an on-colour icon with no state in the CSS.
ours: The bar is 8, 12 and 16px high on a border-neutral-secondary track. Success and Error add a round on-colour icon beside the helper text. value={null} is indeterminate (a pulsing bar, still when motion is reduced; a turning arc on the circle).
reason: The frame heights fit these bars with the label and helper text. The fill colours come from the icon-* tokens, which flip in dark mode, because the DGA background-primary, -success and -error fills are 1.9 to 2.2:1 on the dark track (needs 3:1).

item: Rating: gold fill, hard-coded colour and interaction
original: .rating colour #faaf00 (hard-coded); Figma background-secondary (#dba102) is 2.30:1 on white. Whole stars only, no hover, focus or read-only state.
ours: The fill is background-secondary (or background-primary with brand); every star is outlined in icon-warning (5.43:1) or icon-primary, and an empty star in icon-default-500. Interactive ratings are a radio group with arrow keys, hover preview and a focus ring; read-only ones are an image with a text alternative. Whole stars only, as DGA defines (no half stars).
reason: A graphical object that carries information needs 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11): the outline gives the star its shape at 3:1 or more where the gold fill alone cannot. A rating also has to work by keyboard and be announced.

item: List: physical margins and hard-coded colours
original: .list { margin-left: 24px }, .list--unordered>ul { margin-left: 18px } and list colours #1b8354, #0d121c and #fff written as hex, with --Link-2-link-default_on-color as the on-colour.
ours: Logical margins (ms-6), so a nested list indents from the start side in Arabic. Colours are text-primary, text-default and text-oncolor-primary with icon-primary, icon-default and icon-oncolor. Ordered markers are 1- then a-, with Arabic letters in Arabic.
reason: A margin-left puts the indent on the wrong side in RTL, and hex values do not follow dark mode.

item: Card: border fallback, disabled overlay and link pattern
original: .card { border: 2px solid var(--Colors-Base-black, #fff) } (a white fallback for a black token); .card.disabled fades a gray overlay at .3 opacity over a transparent card; max-width 350px.
ours: A transparent 1px border (a neutral stroke with the stroke effect) and a 2px outline for keyboard focus, so focus does not move the layout. Disabled uses the Figma tokens: background-disabled, text-default-disabled and border-disabled. No fixed width. The clickable card is a real link in the title whose click area is stretched over the card, with the actions raised above it.
reason: The Figma tokens are the source of truth where the CSS disagrees. A card that is only an onclick div has no link semantics (WCAG 4.1.2); the stretched link keeps one link named by the title and a focus ring around the whole card.

original: Selectable Selected = True differs from False only by the checkbox. Figma gives the focused fill as neutral-50 with a black border.
ours: A selected card also gets a 1px border-primary (4.75:1) so the selection does not depend on a 20px checkbox alone.
reason: WCAG 1.4.11: the selected state is a state indicator and needs a clear cue.

item: Pagination: no states, selected style or small-screen form
original: Only sizes (24, 32, 40px) and a gap of 8px; no hover, pressed, selected or disabled styles, no ellipsis or previous and next, and no behaviour on small screens.
ours: Items are transparent with the button neutral hover and pressed fills; the current page is the primary fill with an on-colour label; previous and next are chevrons that mirror in RTL and disable at the ends; skipped pages are an ellipsis; below the sm width the numbers fold into a compact 'page of count'.
reason: A pagination without a current-page style cannot be used. The states follow the Button, which DGA does define.

item: Breadcrumb: separator, current page and collapse
original: Only link-neutral text (Text sm), an icon-default-400 icon (2.5:1 on white), and 2, 3, 4, 5 and more-than-5 levels. No current-page style, no collapse behaviour.
ours: The chevron separator stays icon-default-400: it is decorative and hidden from screen readers. The current page is Medium text-default with aria-current. Above five levels, and below the sm width, the levels between the first and the last two fold behind an ellipsis button that shows the full path.
reason: A chain of five or more levels overflows a phone, and the Figma '>5' variant implies a fold. The ellipsis is a real button, reachable by keyboard.

item: Table of Content: width and height rule
original: .table-of-content is 228px wide, and a second rule sets width: 100% and height: 100vh, which overrides it.
ours: 228px at most (max-w-57) and as tall as its items. The active section is Semibold text-default and aria-current='location'; Up, Down, Home and End move between links.
reason: A 100vh column cannot sit beside content that scrolls, and Figma shows the 228px width.

item: Table: compact sizes, sort and filter buttons
original: Compact is a boolean with no heights; the Sort and Filter header buttons are 20px with five states and no accessible name or aria-sort.
ours: Rows 64px (48px compact), header 48px (40px compact). TableSortButton and TableFilterButton are real buttons with an accessible name; the heading carries aria-sort. The table scrolls sideways inside a region that takes keyboard focus.
reason: A sortable column must say how it is sorted (WCAG 4.1.2), and scrolling content must be reachable without a mouse (WCAG 2.1.1).

original: Selectable rows have Default, Hovered, Focused and Disabled states but no control or semantics; the focus border is table-cell-border-inverse.
ours: A selectable list is a radio group: each row has a radio button (named by the row's label), the arrow keys move between rows, and the chosen row uses table-background-row-select. The focus ring is table-cell-border-inverse, inside the row.
reason: A choice among rows needs a form control behind it for keyboard and screen reader users.

item: Data Table: new, no DGA source
original: DGA has a Table and a Pagination and no data table.
ours: DataTable composes the DGA Table and Pagination with TanStack Table: sorting, a global filter, row selection, pagination, loading rows, an empty state and sideways scrolling. It uses only the Table tokens.
reason: Listed here so nobody looks for it in Figma. It adds no colour: every token is one the Table already uses.

item: Figma variant names: Mideum, Nex/Prev, 2ndry Date, quarterary
original: Carousel Controls Size "Mideum"; Date cell property "Nex/Prev" and "2ndry Date"; the token text-quarterary.
ours: md, outside (a day in the next or previous month), secondaryDate. text-quarterary is not used.
reason: Typos and abbreviations in Figma names. Prop values in code are spelled out.

item: Header: skip link, current page and keyboard
original: Nav Header, Header Menu Item and Header Action are drawn as states only. There is no skip link, no current-page markup, no keyboard model for the sub-menus, and the CSS (.header-nav) sets only the height and padding.
ours: A skip link is the first tab stop. The page the person is on is aria-current="page", and a parent whose child is current takes the selected fill. Left and Right (swapped in RTL), Home and End move between items; the sub-menu is the DGA Menu (Enter, Space or Down opens it, Escape closes it and returns focus).
reason: Bypass blocks (WCAG 2.4.1), current-page information (1.3.1, 2.4.8) and keyboard operation (2.1.1) are not met by a states-only drawing.

original: Nav Header has three variants: under 600, 600 to 960 and over 960.
ours: The navigation sits in the bar from the lg width (1024px) and moves into the Drawer below it. The sm, md and lg widths are the same as every other Platform Code component.
reason: One set of breakpoints for all components. At 960px the main navigation with sub-menus and the actions do not fit one row of the 1280px bar without wrapping.

item: Header: official site strip, Header Menu and Nav Drawer composed
original: The official site strip is the separate Digital Stamp component, and the Second Nav Header is the strip above the primary navigation. Header Menu (a chevron button) and the Nav Drawer are separate components.
ours: Header takes a `stamp` slot for the Digital Stamp (0.7.0) and a `top` slot for a Second Nav, and renders no strip of its own. The chevron is part of the menu item and the sub-menu is the DGA Menu. On narrow screens the navigation is the DGA Drawer with expandable parents; Level 2 links are indented.
reason: Reusing Menu and Drawer keeps the focus, dismissal and mirroring behaviour in one place instead of copying it into the header.

item: Header, Nav Drawer: selected item text is a background token
original: Nav Drawer Item Selected uses fg:background-primary (the brand fill) for the label on button-background-neutral-selected: 3.84:1.
ours: The selected item label uses link-primary-pressed (brand 800), 4.5:1 or better, and the item is Semibold.
reason: Text needs 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3). A fill token is also the wrong token for text.

item: Second Nav: contextual strip, links and scrolling
original: Second Nav Header is a 40px strip with fixed Show Item 2, 3 and 4 and Show Action 2, 3 and 4 switches, a divider and Gray or Primary. It is described as navigation, but the items are text with an icon (a date, the weather).
ours: Items and actions are arrays. An entry is plain text, a link (`href`), or a button (`onClick`), and `current` sets aria-current="page" so it can also be a row of sibling-page links. The strip scrolls sideways on narrow screens instead of wrapping or clipping.
reason: A fixed number of switches cannot hold real content, and a 40px strip that wraps would grow. Links need a current state (WCAG 2.4.8).

item: Footer: hard-coded colours, 72px heading and no mobile form
original: .footer sets --colors-gray-neutral-100, --colors-brand-900 and hsla(var(--colors-alpha-white)/30%) directly, and .footer-title-description h3 is 72px / 90px with a 24px paragraph at every width. Figma has a <600 variant that only changes the weight to Semibold.
ours: Semantic tokens (background-neutral-100, background-sa-flag, alpha-white-30), no 72px heading (the description is Text md and you place any hero text yourself), and below the sm width the link columns fold into the DGA Accordion, one section per column.
reason: Hard-coded values skip the dark theme. A 72px heading overflows a 375px screen. Four link columns at 375px are unreadable.

item: Footer: link semantics and on-colour states
original: The footer has no states for its links, social icons or accordion, and the green variant has no hover, pressed or focus colour.
ours: Links underline on hover and press; social icons have the neutral hover and pressed fills (the transparent on-colour fills on green); focus is a 2px outline (black on gray, white on green). External links get an icon and a screen-reader note.
reason: Every interactive element needs a visible focus (WCAG 2.4.7) and a hover state to match the other links.

item: Date Picker: two sets of hover rules, opacity for disabled
original: The CSS defines .date-cell:hover twice, first with gray-neutral-200 and then with datecell-today-background-hovered, and the today and chosen fills with both brand-600 and text-success. Disabled is opacity .5 on the class and .3 on the attribute.
ours: One set: the datecell tokens from Figma for hover, pressed, chosen and range, text-default-disabled for a disabled day (a chosen disabled day keeps its fill). No opacity.
reason: Opacity makes the contrast of a disabled or chosen day depend on what is behind it, and two conflicting rule sets give different colours depending on the order of the CSS.

item: Date Picker: RTL range band and fixed widths
original: The range band is a 52x48 pseudo-element with a border-radius that [dir=rtl] rules swap by hand, and the inputs are 50px or 200px wide.
ours: The band is the cell's own background, a hard-edged gradient that flips with the direction (to the right in LTR, to the left in RTL), and the cells shrink to fit seven columns in the viewport.
reason: A fixed-width pseudo-element leaves gaps between cells when the cell size changes and needs a second rule per direction.

item: Date Picker: calendars, grid semantics and typing
original: Figma draws a Gregorian calendar with a Secondary Date, a year dropdown and an Input field, and gives no behaviour. There is no Hijri calendar and no keyboard model.
ours: A switch between Gregorian and Hijri (Umm al-Qura, from Intl; years 1300 to 1600 AH). Dates are ISO strings. The month is a role=grid with column headers, aria-selected, aria-current="date" and a full date as the name of each day; one day is in the tab order, arrows, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End move, and Left and Right swap in RTL. Dates can be typed as YYYY-MM-DD (any digits) and are checked against min, max and disabled dates.
reason: A date picker must be usable without a pointer (WCAG 2.1.1), and Saudi forms need both calendars.

item: Date Picker: days in the next and previous month
original: Date cell has a Nex/Prev switch and a Null state.
ours: In one month the days of the neighbouring months are shown in text-secondary-paragraph and can be chosen. In the dual-month view they are left empty, so no date appears twice.
reason: Two months side by side would otherwise show the same date in both grids.

item: Carousel: autoplay, pause and reduced motion
original: Carousel has three styles (Arrows, Dots, Dots Only) and no behaviour. Moving content is not addressed.
ours: Autoplay is off by default. When it is on, a pause button is always shown, it stops while the pointer or focus is inside, and it does not start when the person prefers reduced motion. The live region is off while it plays and polite when it does not.
reason: Moving content that starts by itself must be pausable (WCAG 2.2.2), and a live region that fires on every slide would make a screen reader unusable.

item: Carousel: dots are 8 to 16px and distinguished by colour only
original: Carousel Controls are 16, 12 or 8px squares in a Selected or not state with no colour given.
ours: The dot is drawn 8, 12 or 16px, inside a 24px button. The chosen dot is filled and the others are rings, so it does not rely on colour.
reason: A target should be 24px (WCAG 2.5.8) and state should not be shown by colour alone (1.4.1).

original: Carousel Arrows have Direction Left and Right and an RTL variant for each.
ours: Previous and next. The icon mirrors, the first slide is on the right in RTL, the track moves the other way, the arrow keys swap and a swipe is read by the page direction.
reason: One component for both directions instead of mirrored copies; the slide order follows reading order.

item: Filtration: the panel and the mobile form are designed here
original: Filtration is a 123x40 trigger with Open, Result and Show Results flags and Placement Center, Right and Left. The internal parts (_Filtration list, _Multi Select Checkbox Filter, _Text Range) are not drawn.
ours: A panel of checkbox, radio, select, input and range groups beside the results from lg, applied filters as removable Tags with clear all, a result count, and below lg the same panel in the DGA Drawer from a button. Placement is the drawer side (start or end), with no centred dialog.
reason: The spec has the button only. The panel is composed from the DGA Checkbox, Radio, Select, Input, Tag and Drawer so it needs no new colour.

ours: Extension, new, no DGA source: the DGA Menu surface (background-menu, border, radius-md, shadow-2xl) with the Tooltip beak
reason: There is no DGA specification to compare it with. It adds no token: every colour comes from an existing DGA token.

ours: Extension, new, no DGA source: the Popover surface, opened by hover or focus on a primary link
reason: There is no DGA specification to compare it with. It adds no token: every colour comes from an existing DGA token.

ours: Extension, new, no DGA source: the DGA Dialog (Modal) with the alert dialog behaviour and the Button
reason: There is no DGA specification to compare it with. It adds no token: every colour comes from an existing DGA token.

ours: Extension, new, no DGA source: the DGA Menu list, opened by right-click, long-press or the Menu key
reason: There is no DGA specification to compare it with. It adds no token: every colour comes from an existing DGA token.

item: Slider track, fill and thumb colours
original: The Figma Slider page lists only the label and helper text tokens (field-text-label)
ours: Track --control-border, fill and thumb --control-primary-checked (hovered and pressed variants), thumb ring --control-thumb
reason: The spec gives no colours for the track and thumb. The Switch control tokens are reused, so the track and the fill are 3:1 or better on every surface (WCAG 1.4.11) in light and dark. No new token.

item: Toggle and Toggle Group pressed state
original: Not defined by DGA (the Button has aria-pressed fills in the spec)
ours: The Button selected fill plus a 1px --border-black border
reason: The Button selected fill is background-neutral-selected, which is 1.2:1 against the page in light mode, so a pressed toggle would be told apart by colour alone. The dark border (3:1 or better) is a second cue. Uses an existing token: new behaviour, no new colour.

ours: Field, arrow and clear button from Input and Select; list from Select; chips from the neutral Tag.
reason: New, no DGA source. DGA has no searchable select. Every colour is an existing DGA token and no token was added.

ours: A create row with a plus icon when the typed text matches no option.
reason: New, no DGA source. shadcn's registry has no creatable combobox; the behaviour follows Base UI's creatable recipe.

ours: Search Box over a Menu-style list of actions, with a dialog form.
reason: New, no DGA source. DGA has no command menu. Items follow Menu; a 2px start bar marks the highlighted action because focus stays in the search box and the Menu tint alone is 1.1:1. No token was added.

item: Digital Stamp: wording, flag icon and the https and registration rows
original: Figma draws the 32px strip, its opened state and the domain Extension part; no text
ours: English defaults for every string (all props), a Hugeicons flag, lock and security-check icon, and three rows in the opened panel.
reason: New, no DGA source. The spec gives the layout and tokens, not the wording or artwork. The wording is ours; DGA's registration and domain purposes are taken from the spec's description.

item: Digital Stamp: opened state and mobile layout
